key_insight: RAPO improves offline RL by adapting policy regularization separately for value-learning and action-execution roles instead of forcing one shared policy coefficient.
engineering_relevance: The method offers a practical way to stabilize offline policy optimization by tuning actor regularization where it matters most in the learning pipeline.
method: Differentiates through candidate policy updates built from the base actor objective to learn role-specific coefficients.
For TD3+BC, splits bootstrap and execution actors and adapts their coefficients independently.
For IQL, keeps value learning unchanged and adapts only the inverse temperature used for advantage-weighted policy extraction.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports experiments on D4RL locomotion and AntMaze benchmarks, with RAPO outperforming the base algorithms and especially improving TD3+BC on average.
watch_item: RAPO adds an extra meta-optimization step, so implementation complexity and sensitivity to update stability may matter in practice.
paper_title: Role-Adaptive Policy Optimization for Offline Reinforcement Learning
